detail: Ministry register identifies the monumental projecting western entrance, twin end minarets, courtyard arcades and central fountain.

Museum lists the 120 by 113 m enclosure and 78 by 66 m courtyard. It describes masonry piers, five arcades on the eastern qibla side, two on the west and three on each other side. Only the middle dome survives from the three originally built.
The Aga Khan inventory records the brick arcades, stone exterior, square protective cases around the different minaret shafts, higher central prayer axis and mihrab dome on squinches.
The state press service records the mosque reopening following its 2023 restoration.
The museum identifies both minarets in Girault de Prangey’s composite. It dates both replacement tops to the restoration after the 1303 earthquake.
